topic: SC: certified green crackers allowed in Delhi-NCR only on 7 and 8 Nov 2026 (6-7 AM and 8-10 PM); QR-coded NEERI-approved green crackers only, no online sale, no ladis or barium crackers, no-cracker zones within 300 m of hospitals, old-age homes and silence zones; ban resumes 9 Nov (Arjun Gopal v. Union of India, 2026 LiveLaw (SC) 1115, Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale, 2 Nov 2026)

slides.title: Crackers in Delhi-NCR: **two days**, fixed hours
slides.subtitle: Only **certified green crackers**, only on **7 and 8 November**.
slides.cite: **Arjun Gopal v. Union of India** · 2026 LiveLaw (SC) 1115

slides.label: When you can burst
slides.title: Two days, **three hours** a day
bullets: Allowed only on **7 and 8 November 2026** in Delhi-NCR.
Time slots: **6 AM to 7 AM** and **8 PM to 10 PM**, on both days.
From **9 November**, the full ban on crackers comes back.

slides.label: Which crackers
slides.title: Green, **certified**, and QR-coded
bullets: Only green crackers approved by **CSIR-NEERI**, made by makers holding NEERI and **PESO** certification.
Boxes must carry a **QR code** showing the maker, licence and test certificate.
**Ladis** (crackers joined in a series), garlands and crackers with **barium** are not allowed. **Online sale** is banned.

slides.label: Where not to burst
slides.title: Respect the **no-cracker zones**
bullets: No crackers within **300 metres** of hospitals, nursing homes, health centres, old-age homes and notified **silence zones**.
Educational institutions are also to be marked as **no-cracker zones**.
Police must check sale points, scan QR codes, seize illegal crackers and prosecute offending makers and traders.
slides.note: **Law fact:** the court said freedom of religion is subject to **public health** and the right to clean air under **Article 21**.

slides.label: Keep in mind
slides.title: This is **not** the end of the ban
bullets: The court called this a **temporary** relaxation, not a lifting of the ban.
It warned that officials who fail to enforce the order may face **contempt** action.
This post is for information only, not legal advice.

caption:
Planning to burst crackers this Diwali in Delhi-NCR? Read the Supreme Court's rules first 🪔⚖️

On 2 November 2026, the Supreme Court allowed only certified green crackers in Delhi-NCR, and only on 7 and 8 November, from 6 AM to 7 AM and from 8 PM to 10 PM. The full ban returns on 9 November. The court made clear this is a temporary relaxation, not the end of the ban.

Only CSIR-NEERI approved green crackers in boxes with a QR code are allowed. Ladis (crackers joined in a series), garlands, barium crackers and online sales are not allowed. No crackers within 300 metres of hospitals, nursing homes, health centres, old-age homes and notified silence zones, and educational institutions are also to be marked as no-cracker zones.

Police must check sale points, verify QR codes, seize illegal crackers and prosecute offending makers and traders. The court warned officials of contempt action if its order is not enforced, and said religious freedom is subject to public health and the right to clean air under Article 21.

Case: Arjun Gopal & Ors. v. Union of India & Ors., 2026 LiveLaw (SC) 1115 (2 Nov 2026)
Bench: Justice MM Sundresh and Justice PB Varale
